sources.title: Fear extinction as a model for translational neuroscience: ten years of progress
sources.relevance: Foundational review linking extinction neuroscience to translational PTSD research; key evidence for vmPFC role in extinction recall

sources.title: The neurocircuitry of fear, stress, and anxiety disorders
sources.relevance: Comprehensive cross-disorder neuroimaging review; establishes amygdala hyperactivity and vmPFC hypoactivity as consistent PTSD findings

sources.authors: Rauch SL, Shin LM, Phelps EA
sources.title: Neurocircuitry models of posttraumatic stress disorder and extinction: human neuroimaging research--past, present, and future
sources.relevance: Foundational neurocircuitry model of PTSD proposing amygdala hyperreactivity + frontal/hippocampal deficit

sources.authors: Maren S, Phan KL, Liberzon I
sources.title: The contextual brain: implications for fear conditioning, extinction and psychopathology
sources.relevance: Key review on hippocampal contextual gating in fear/extinction; explains PTSD's extinction generalization failure and trauma context over-generalization

sources.authors: Milad MR, Pitman RK, Ellis CB, Gold AL, Shin LM, Lasko NB, Zeidan MA, Handwerger K, Orr SP, Rauch SL
sources.title: Neurobiological basis of failure to recall extinction memory in posttraumatic stress disorder
sources.relevance: THE key experiment: PTSD patients learn extinction normally (Day 1) but fail to recall it (Day 2); vmPFC hypoactivity during recall is the neural correlate

sources.authors: Pitman RK, Rasmusson AM, Koenen KC, Shin LM, Orr SP, Gilbertson MW, Milad MR, Liberzon I
sources.title: Biological studies of post-traumatic stress disorder
sources.relevance: Comprehensive review of 30 years of PTSD biology; hippocampal volume, HPA cortisol paradox, genetics, epigenetics, reconsolidation

sources.authors: Ressler KJ, Berretta S, Bolshakov VY, Rosso IM, Meloni EG, Rauch SL, Carlezon WA Jr.
sources.title: Post-traumatic stress disorder: clinical and translational neuroscience from cells to circuits
sources.relevance: Most recent comprehensive review; epidemiology (6-8%), genetics (30-40% heritability), multi-omics integration, circuit-to-treatment framework
